title: Landforms, Mass Movement and Soil Erosion
summary: Landforms made by erosion and deposition, the stages of a river, types of mass movement, and the causes, effects and prevention of soil erosion.

notes.text: In the **Karoo**, layers of soft sedimentary rock are capped by hard **dolerite**. As the softer rock is eroded, the hard cap protects the land beneath it, forming flat-topped hills.

items: **Plateau**: a large, high area with a flat top.
**Mesa**: a flat-topped hill with steep sides, wider than it is high (formed as a plateau is eroded).
**Butte**: a smaller hill, higher than it is wide.
**Conical hill**: when the cap rock is removed, the hill is worn into a cone shape.

rows: Flood plains, oxbow lakes, levees, deltas

notes.text: A bend in a river. Water flows fastest on the outside of the bend, eroding a river cliff; it is slowest on the inside, depositing a slip-off slope. Meanders can be cut off to form oxbow lakes.
A fan-shaped area of deposited sediment at a river mouth, formed where the river slows down on entering the sea or a lake (e.g. the Nile Delta and the Okavango inland delta).
The downhill movement of rock and soil under the influence of gravity, often triggered by heavy rain, earthquakes or human activity.

rows: Soil moves slowly downslope; shows as tilted fences, poles and trees
Saturated soil flows like a liquid after very heavy rain
A mass of rock and soil slides down a slope along a slip plane
Rocks break off a cliff and fall freely, often after frost action

notes.text: **Soil erosion** is the removal of fertile topsoil by water or wind faster than new soil can form. It is a serious problem in South Africa: in parts of the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal deep gullies called **dongas** have formed.

rows: Planting trees and grass; keeping vegetation cover
Cover crops, mulching, gabions (wire baskets of stones) in gullies

items: **Effects**: loss of fertile soil and lower crop yields; dams and rivers silt up; increased flooding; food insecurity and poverty.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: On an orthophoto map, look for light-coloured, branching lines without vegetation on slopes: these are often dongas (gullies) caused by soil erosion.

questions.prompt: Give THREE causes of soil erosion.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): overgrazing; deforestation; ploughing down slopes; heavy rain on bare soil; poor road drainage; veld fires

questions.prompt: Suggest THREE ways farmers can prevent soil erosion.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): contour ploughing; terracing; rotational grazing; planting cover crops/trees; gabions; mulching

questions.prompt: Name TWO factors that can trigger a landslide.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): heavy rain; earthquakes; removing vegetation; building/cutting into slopes; mining; undercutting by rivers or waves
